elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (i): "the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards" — an affirmative TrueLink warranty covering both defined service streams.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (ii): "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (ii) runs "for twelve (12) months following delivery."

Inserted clause (i) runs "for ninety (90) days following performance." The tense ("will be performed" within a look-back window) is slightly awkward drafting, but the operative period is unambiguously 90 days for the Services warranty.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Remedy sentence: "TrueLink will, at its option, repair or replace the non-conforming software, re-perform the non-conforming services..." — at Vendor's option is consistent with the playbook model language.
Remedy sentence closes "...or refund the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (iii): "TrueLink will comply with all applicable laws in performing this Agreement."

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (iv): "the Interface, all related software and all materials delivered to Client hereunder are free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code."

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Twelve (12) months of documentation conformance for the Interface and related software exceeds the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Ninety (90) days for the Hosting and Support Services exceeds the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replace the non-conforming software, re-perform the non-conforming services" appears in the same inserted remedy sentence.
"or refund the fees paid for them."

reasons: The single inserted paragraph appended to Section 9 covers all eight preferred elements in operative language (professional/workmanlike Services for 90 days, 12-month software conformance to documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) plus the full repair/replace, re-perform or refund remedy, so the preferred level is position-complete and the fallback is satisfied a fortiori.

Nothing material is left to the margin comment: the 90/30 fallback is offered only as an alternative and every preferred term is rendered in the clause text, so no element depends on the comment or an undefined trigger.

Minimal: the drafter added one paragraph and touched nothing else. The existing Y2K warranty (Section 9), the Section 11 standard of care and the disclaimer are retained verbatim, and no requirement outside the WARRANTY checklist (e.g., no acceptance-testing, escrow, SLA credit or exclusive-remedy language) is smuggled in.
Correctly no carve-out edit to the disclaimer: p0076 already opens "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so the express warranty is not swallowed and further amendment would be surplus.

Preserves intent: the new warranty is cumulative with, and does not contradict, Section 11's standard of care; the remedy is at TrueLink's option (matching the model language) and is not stated to be exclusive, so it does not disturb other remedies, timing or commercial mechanics.

Optional polish only, not a defect: clause (i) reads "for ninety (90) days following performance, the ... Services will be performed..."; "will have been performed" would be cleaner, and the paragraph could carry its own subsection number rather than trailing the Y2K text. Neither affects the operative period or remedy.
